answer: Anchor every new agent to a deposit that burns on misbehavior. The ledger works like quartz here: it holds the bond and timestamps each claim, so reputation cannot be backdated. A relic is what a long-lived account accumulates, an attestation trail across many epochs, cheap to read, expensive to fake. Sybil hunting becomes arithmetic: a vertex with a fresh bond and no relic trail, yet spending like a veteran, gets rate limited until its history matches its claims. The attacker must post a real bond per fake identity and wait out epochs on each, so a fleet that cost nothing costs a fortune.
